lessons.title: Schutz, schützen, Umweltschutz: learning words in families
lessons.goal: Learn words in families: find the stem, read the word class from the ending, understand prefixes and compounds, and use four steps to learn ten words at once.

grammar.topic: Word families: stem, suffix, prefix and compound
grammar.point: No new grammar, but a way of learning words. A family grows from one stem. Endings show the word class: -ung, -heit and -keit make feminine nouns, -lich, -ig and -bar make adjectives. Prefixes such as ver-, ab-, wieder- and um- change the meaning. In a compound the last part decides the article.

mistake.why: The last part of a compound decides the article: der Schutz, so der Umweltschutz.

terms.meaning: a group of words that share the same stem: schützen, der Schutz, geschützt
the core part of a word that carries the meaning: schütz-
a small part in front of the stem that changes the meaning: ver-, ab-, wieder-
a small part at the end that shows the word class: -ung, -keit, -lich
a compound: two or more words joined into one; the last part decides the article

cards.title: Before we start: from one word to a family
cards.body: This lesson has no new grammar. It teaches a way of learning. At Datenhafen Mira builds the app „Grüner Kiez“ and needs many new words. Learning them one by one is slow. Words belong to families, and a family is easier to learn than a list.
steps: You already know: Wir wollen die Umwelt schützen. You know the verb schützen from this chapter.
New today: Der Umweltschutz ist wichtig. The same stem, now as a noun, and a whole family around it.
By the end you can: find the stem of a word, guess the word class and the article from an ending, and learn a word family in four steps.

examples.de: Wir wollen die Umwelt schützen.
examples.en: We want to protect the environment.
examples.why: You know this: the verb schützen.

examples.de: Der Umweltschutz ist wichtig.
examples.en: Environmental protection is important.
examples.why: New today: a noun from the same family.

cards.more: Picture a family photo. You do not need a new name tag for every person, because many of them look alike: same nose, same smile. Words in a family look alike too. They share a core, the stem, and only the ends or the front parts change. If you know one face, you can often recognise the cousins. Today you learn to see the family resemblance, and every new word stops being a stranger.

cards.title: Thirty words in one afternoon
cards.body: Mira has to collect thirty words for the app „Grüner Kiez“. Leon watches her work and asks how she does it. Her answer: not one by one, but in families. Read the dialogue and notice the word Wortfamilie.
cards.lead: Before any rules, a scene. Mira explains her trick to Leon in the kitchen. Read the six lines and spot the words that look alike. The next cards show how the trick works.

examples.de: Mira muss für die App dreißig Wörter sammeln.
examples.en: Mira has to collect thirty words for the app.

examples.de: Sie lernt die Wörter nicht einzeln, sondern in Familien.
examples.en: She does not learn the words one by one, but in families.

examples.de: Mit einem Wort lernst du oft drei andere.
examples.en: With one word you often learn three others.

deeper.text: German children learn word families already in primary school, so for Germans this trick is normal. Teachers write a stem on the board and the class collects the relatives. Zur Familie von fahren gehören zum Beispiel die Fahrt, der Fahrer und das Fahrrad. You use the same method as a school child, only in your second language.

example.de: Zur Familie von fahren gehören die Fahrt, der Fahrer und das Fahrrad.
example.en: The family of fahren includes die Fahrt, der Fahrer and das Fahrrad.

cards.more: Think of a shopping trolley. You can push thirty single apples into it one by one, or you can put them into one bag and push the bag. A family is the bag. When you pick up the stem schütz-, you carry the verb, the noun and the adjective together. Mira does exactly that: she learns the stem once and pulls the relatives out of the bag when she needs them. That saves her hours.
steps: Mira: Ich brauche dreißig Wörter für die App „Grüner Kiez“.
Leon: Dreißig? Das ist viel Arbeit!
Mira: Nein, ich lerne sie in Familien. Schau: schützen, der Schutz, der Umweltschutz.
Leon: Das ist ja dasselbe Wort mit anderen Teilen!
Mira: Genau. Das gehört zur selben Familie.
Leon: Dann mache ich auch eine Familie: kochen, der Koch, die Köchin.

cards.title: The family tree of schütz-
cards.body: A word family grows from one stem. Here the stem is schütz-. Around it you find a verb, nouns and an adjective. All of them are about protecting. Learn the stem once, and the others become easy to guess.
cards.lead: Mira starts with the family you already half know. This card shows the whole tree of schütz-, with each member and its word class, so that you can see how one stem produces many words.

examples.de: Wir schützen die Umwelt.
examples.en: We protect the environment.

examples.de: Der Naturschutz ist ein wichtiges Thema.
examples.en: Nature conservation is an important topic.

examples.de: Im Schutzgebiet sind viele Pflanzen geschützt.
examples.en: In the protected area many plants are protected.

deeper.text: Members of a family bring their friends along. The verb schützen goes with vor and the dative: Bäume schützen uns vor der Hitze. The noun does the same: der Schutz vor Regen. So when you learn one member, learn the little word that sticks to it, and you get a ready-made chunk for free.

example.de: Ein Gründach schützt das Haus vor Hitze.
example.en: A green roof protects the house from heat.

cards.more: Draw the stem as the trunk of a tree. The verb is one branch, the nouns grow on a second branch, and the adjective hangs on a third. Every leaf is a word. If you stand under the tree and look up, you see that all the leaves belong to the same trunk. That is why a new leaf does not scare you: you already know the trunk. Mira draws such a tree for every stem in her notebook.

cards.title: Endings tell the word class
cards.body: The end of a word often shows what it is. -ung, -heit and -keit make feminine nouns: die Trennung, die Sauberkeit. -lich, -ig and -bar make adjectives: natürlich, schmutzig, wiederverwendbar. Look at the end, and you know the article or the word class before you open a dictionary.
cards.lead: The family tree showed many members. How do you tell a noun from an adjective in a new word? The ending helps. This card gives the endings that appear most often in the topic of the environment.

examples.de: Die Erwärmung der Erde ist ein großes Problem.
examples.en: The warming of the earth is a big problem.

examples.de: Sauberkeit ist für alle wichtig.
examples.en: Cleanliness is important for everyone.

examples.de: Der Becher ist wiederverwendbar.
examples.en: The cup is reusable.

deeper.text: The suffix -keit has a rule and a famous exception. After -ig, -lich, -bar and -sam you always get -keit: die Wichtigkeit, die Sparsamkeit. With other stems you often find -heit: die Gesundheit, die Freiheit. The word sauber is one of the exceptions: die Sauberkeit. So the family helps you guess, but exceptions you simply learn.

example.de: Alle sprechen über die Wichtigkeit des Umweltschutzes.
example.en: Everybody talks about the importance of environmental protection.

cards.more: Think of a train. The engine is the stem, and the last carriage is the ending. By looking at the last carriage you see where the train belongs: an -ung carriage belongs to the feminine nouns, a -lich carriage belongs to the adjectives. You do not need to read the whole train. A quick glance at the end is enough. With some practice you will do it automatically when you read a new text.

cards.title: Front parts change the meaning
cards.body: A prefix stands in front of the stem and changes the meaning. ver- often means wrong or used up: verschmutzen, verbrauchen. ab- often means away or finished: abgelaufen. wieder- means again: wiederverwenden. um- means around: die Umwelt, the world around us.
cards.lead: Endings give the word class. Now look at the front of the word. Four small prefixes open the door to many words in this chapter. Each one has a basic meaning that you can use to guess.

examples.de: Der Joghurt ist abgelaufen.
examples.en: The yoghurt has expired.

examples.de: Wir können den Becher wiederverwenden.
examples.en: We can use the cup again.

examples.de: Plastik verschmutzt das Meer.
examples.en: Plastic pollutes the sea.

deeper.text: The prefix ver- often points to something that goes wrong or too far: verschmutzen (make dirty), verschwenden (waste). You know the same pattern from A2: Mira hat sich im Kiez verlaufen means she took the wrong way and got lost. When you meet an unknown ver- word with a negative feeling, wrong or too much is a good first guess.

example.de: Mira hat sich im Kiez verlaufen.
example.en: Mira got lost in the Kiez.

cards.more: Imagine small building blocks. The stem is a big block, and a prefix is a small coloured block you put in front. A blue block ver- turns the stem into something negative, a red block wieder- adds the idea of repeating. You do not need to learn a new big block each time. You only remember what each colour means. With four colours you can already build and understand dozens of words.

cards.title: Compounds: the last word decides
cards.body: German joins nouns into compounds. The last part is the main word, and it decides the article: die Umwelt + der Schutz = der Umweltschutz, because der Schutz. The first part only describes it. If you know the article of the last word, you know the article of the whole compound.
cards.lead: Many environmental words are compounds. This card shows how to read them from the back: the last part names the thing and gives the article, and the first part tells you which kind it is.

examples.de: Der Umweltschutz beginnt im Alltag.
examples.en: Environmental protection begins in everyday life.

examples.de: Die Mülltrennung ist in Deutschland sehr wichtig.
examples.en: Waste separation is very important in Germany.

examples.de: Das Schutzgebiet liegt am Fluss.
examples.en: The protected area lies on the river.

deeper.text: Sometimes a small -s- sits between the two parts: Arbeit + s + Weg gives der Arbeitsweg. Schutz + Gebiet has no such letter. There is no complete rule for the linking -s-. So do not try to construct compounds freely at the start. Learn each compound as one word, with its article, and you will get it right.

example.de: Der Arbeitsweg dauert zwanzig Minuten.
example.en: The way to work takes twenty minutes.

cards.more: Think of a train again, but now each carriage is a whole word. The front carriages describe, and the last carriage is the one the passengers actually use. In der Glascontainer the container is the thing, the glass only says which kind. If someone asks you which article to take, you always look at the last carriage. That one carriage is the boss, and the others obey.

cards.title: How to learn a family
cards.body: Four steps turn a family into a habit. First find the stem. Then collect four to six members. Then write the article and the word class. Finally write one sentence for each word. Mira does this for every stem in her notebook, and she learns about ten words in half an hour.
cards.lead: You now know the tools: stem, endings, prefixes and compounds. This last card puts them into a method that you can use with every new word in German, not only in this chapter.

examples.de: Zuerst suche ich den Wortstamm.
examples.en: First I look for the word stem.

examples.de: Dann schreibe ich vier bis sechs Wörter dazu.
examples.en: Then I write four to six words next to it.

examples.de: Zum Schluss mache ich zu jedem Wort einen Satz.
examples.en: In the end I make a sentence for every word.

deeper.text: A family guess is a hint, not a proof. The words brauchen, gebrauchen and verbrauchen belong together, but their meanings are different, and verbrauchen means to use up. So test every guess in a sentence. If the sentence sounds odd, look the word up. Wrong guesses are useful too, because you remember the correction well.

example.de: Eine Lampe verbraucht Strom.
example.en: A lamp uses up electricity.

cards.more: Compare it with tidying a drawer. If you throw forty socks in at once, you cannot find any pair. If you put the pairs together, you find each one in seconds. The four steps are the pairs. Step one finds the first sock, step two finds its partners, step three labels the pile, step four wears them in a sentence. A tidy drawer and a tidy head work the same way: little order, much speed.
steps: 1. Find the stem: schütz-
2. Collect four to six members: schützen, der Schutz, der Naturschutz, das Schutzgebiet, geschützt
3. Mark the article and the word class: der Schutz (noun), geschützt (adjective)
4. Write one sentence for each word: Der Naturschutz beginnt im eigenen Garten.

drills.prompt: ___ Umweltschutz ist wichtig.
drills.hint: Look at the last part of the compound and its article.
drills.explanation: der Schutz decides: der Umweltschutz.

drills.prompt: Make a noun with -ung from the verb entsorgen. (with article)

lessons.title: Was halten wir davon? Ideas for the Kiez
lessons.goal: Discuss ideas for the neighbourhood: say for or against with a reason, weigh two sides, name a condition, disagree politely and report the result.

grammar.topic: Discussing ideas: patterns you already know
grammar.point: No new grammar. For or against: Ich bin dafür, dass … (verb at the end) or, with the same doer, dafür, … zu + infinitive. Two sides: Einerseits + verb, andererseits + verb. A condition: unter einer Bedingung (unter + dative). Objections: Das ist übertrieben. Das ist unsinnig, weil … Result: Wir haben uns auf … geeinigt (sich einigen auf + accusative).
grammar.oneLine: Ich bin dafür, dass wir mit der Aufräumaktion anfangen.

mistake.right: Ich bin dafür, dass wir ein Lastenrad kaufen.
mistake.why: In a dass-clause the verb goes to the end.

terms.meaning: da-words for a whole idea: for it, against it
a condition: I agree only if something happens first
an objection: a reason against an idea
to agree on something together; reflexive verb with auf + accusative

cards.title: Before we start: from 'Ich finde das gut' to 'Ich bin dafür, aber unter einer Bedingung'
cards.body: Frau Weber's club „Viertel hilft“ meets in the Nachbarschaftshaus. The neighbours discuss four ideas for the Kiez, and nobody wants to just say gut or schlecht. This lesson has no new grammar. You put your known tools to work: for and against, two sides, conditions and a result.
steps: You already know: Ich bin dafür, dass wir ein Lastenrad kaufen. and Einerseits … andererseits … from chapter 4.
New today: Das ist übertrieben. and Wir haben uns auf die Aufräumaktion geeinigt. Two new chunks for a real discussion.
By the end you can: say for or against with a reason, weigh two sides, name a condition and report the result.

examples.de: Ich bin dafür, dass wir ein Lastenrad kaufen.
examples.en: I am for us buying a cargo bike.
examples.why: You know this: for something, with dass.

examples.de: Wir haben uns auf die Aufräumaktion geeinigt.
examples.en: We have agreed on the clean-up action.
examples.why: New today: reporting a result.

cards.more: Think of a football referee. In a discussion you are a bit like one: you listen to both teams, you say what counts, and in the end you announce the result. Today you collect the whistles you need: one for yes, one for no, one for yes-but, and one for the final result. You already own most of them. This lesson only puts them in one pocket, so you can reach for them quickly.

cards.title: The „Viertel hilft“ evening
cards.body: Frau Weber leads the evening in the Nachbarschaftshaus. The four flatmates sit in the circle. There are four ideas on the board: a Lastenrad to borrow, a Tauschregal, a Gründach on the Nachbarschaftshaus and a Aufräumaktion. Read the dialogue and notice who is for and who is against what.
cards.lead: Before the phrases, the scene. Read the eight lines of the evening once and underline the opinions. The next cards sort the phrases and give you the tools to use them yourself.

examples.de: Ich bin für das Lastenrad.
examples.en: I am for the cargo bike.

examples.de: Ein Lastenrad ist zu teuer für unseren Verein.
examples.en: A cargo bike is too expensive for our club.

examples.de: Frau Weber stellt vier Ideen für den Kiez vor.
examples.en: Frau Weber presents four ideas for the Kiez.

deeper.text: For a short answer, German does not say Ich bin für es. A thing is replaced by a da-word: dafür and dagegen. Das Lastenrad? Ich bin dafür! The da-word stands alone, without a noun, and it works as a full answer. You can use it in the same way when somebody asks Wer ist dafür? Then you raise your hand and say: Ich!

example.de: Das Lastenrad? Ich bin dafür.
example.en: The cargo bike? I am for it.

cards.more: Imagine a school class voting with colour cards. Green means for, red means against. Frau Weber is the teacher at the front, and the neighbours hold up their cards while they talk. Each of them gives a short reason, so the group sees not only who is green or red, but also why. When you read the dialogue, give each speaker a card colour. It shows you the structure of the evening in seconds.
steps: Frau Weber: Guten Abend! Wir haben vier Ideen für unseren Kiez: ein Lastenrad zum Ausleihen, ein Tauschregal, ein Gründach auf dem Nachbarschaftshaus und eine Aufräumaktion.
Leon: Ich bin für das Lastenrad. Man könnte damit Einkäufe nach Hause bringen.
Mira: Ich bin dagegen. Ein Lastenrad ist zu teuer für unseren Verein.
Anna: Ein Gründach ist schön. Einerseits ist es teuer, andererseits macht es die Häuser kühler.
Ben: Ein ganzes Gründach? Das ist übertrieben für den Anfang.
Frau Weber: Und die Aufräumaktion? Sie ist die billigste und schnellste Maßnahme.
Mira: Dann bin ich dafür, dass wir mit der Aufräumaktion anfangen.
Leon: Gut. Wir haben uns auf die Aufräumaktion geeinigt!

cards.title: For and against
cards.body: To say yes or no, use dafür or dagegen with dass, and name a reason with weil. To list what speaks for or against an idea, name an advantage (ein Vorteil) or a point of criticism (ein Kritikpunkt). The dass-clause and the weil-clause send the verb to the end.
cards.lead: Four patterns cover most of a discussion about an idea: yes with a reason, no with a reason, an advantage and a point of criticism. The table gives them with an example each.

examples.de: Ich bin dafür, dass es ein Tauschregal gibt.
examples.en: I am for there being a swap shelf.

examples.de: Ein Vorteil ist, dass man Bücher teilen kann.
examples.en: One advantage is that you can share books.

examples.de: Ein Kritikpunkt ist der hohe Preis.
examples.en: One point of criticism is the high price.

deeper.text: When you speak for yourself and for the group, the dass-clause can shrink to zu + infinitive: Ich bin dafür, ein Lastenrad zu kaufen. That is shorter and sounds natural. You need dass when somebody else does the action: Ich bin dafür, dass die Stadt ein Lastenrad kauft. The rule is the same as in chapter 1: the zu-part needs a clear doer.

example.de: Ich bin dafür, ein Lastenrad zu kaufen.
example.en: I am for buying a cargo bike.

cards.more: Picture two baskets on a table: one for pro, one for contra. Each pattern in the table is a way of putting a small card into a basket. Dafür drops a card into the green one, dagegen into the red one. Ein Vorteil and ein Kritikpunkt are cards with an argument written on them. A good discussion needs at least one card in each basket before anybody decides. Then the result feels fair.

rows: Ich bin dafür, dass es ein Tauschregal gibt.
Ich bin dagegen, weil das Lastenrad zu teuer ist.
Ein Vorteil ist, dass man Bücher teilen kann.
Ein Kritikpunkt ist der hohe Preis.

cards.title: Weighing two sides
cards.body: Einerseits … andererseits … puts two sides next to each other. Each half is a main clause, so the verb follows straight after einerseits and straight after andererseits. A comma separates the halves. It is the perfect pattern when you cannot yet say yes or no.
cards.lead: Often an idea has good and bad sides. German has a fixed pair of words for this. You know it from chapter 4, and now you use it for the Kiez ideas, with the verb in the right place.

examples.de: Einerseits ist ein Gründach teuer, andererseits macht es die Häuser kühler.
examples.en: On the one hand a green roof is expensive, on the other hand it makes the houses cooler.

examples.de: Einerseits ist das Lastenrad praktisch, andererseits braucht es viel Platz.
examples.en: On the one hand the cargo bike is practical, on the other hand it needs a lot of space.

examples.de: Einerseits möchte ich helfen, andererseits habe ich wenig Zeit.
examples.en: On the one hand I would like to help, on the other hand I have little time.

deeper.text: Weighing usually leads to a decision, and German often marks it with deshalb. Einerseits kostet es Zeit, andererseits spart es Geld. Deshalb bin ich dafür. The first sentence shows the balance, and the short second sentence gives your decision. Without that last step the listener waits for you to say what you actually think.

example.de: Deshalb bin ich dafür.
example.en: That is why I am for it.

cards.more: Imagine an old kitchen scale with two pans. In the left pan you put one argument, in the right pan the other. Einerseits is the left pan, andererseits is the right pan. The sentence is the moment when the scale wobbles. You say both sides, and then you see which side is heavier. Mira and Anna use exactly this picture when they cannot decide yet. The pattern lets you say: both sides are real.
steps: Einerseits + verb: the first side (a good or a bad point).
andererseits + verb: the other side, with a comma before it.
Then your decision: Deshalb bin ich dafür. or Deshalb bin ich dagegen.

cards.title: Conditions and objections
cards.body: Sometimes you agree, but not completely. Then you name a condition: unter einer Bedingung. Sometimes you reject an idea: Das ist übertrieben. Das ist unsinnig, weil … Or you compare it with a better one: eine wirksamere Maßnahme. The table collects the phrases that you need.
cards.lead: Between yes and no there is a large space. These five phrases fill it: agreeing with a condition, saying something is too much, saying it is pointless, saying yes-but, and offering a better measure.

examples.de: Ich bin dafür, aber unter einer Bedingung: Wir fragen zuerst die Nachbarn.
examples.en: I am for it, but on one condition: we ask the neighbours first.

examples.de: Ein ganzes Gründach? Das ist übertrieben!
examples.en: A whole green roof? That is exaggerated!

examples.de: Das ist unsinnig, weil es niemand braucht.
examples.en: That is pointless because nobody needs it.

deeper.text: In unter einer Bedingung the preposition unter takes the dative, and the whole phrase is a fixed chunk that you can learn as one piece. A longer form is unter der Bedingung, dass …, which is a little more formal and ends in a dass-clause. Both forms work in a discussion at the club. The first one is shorter and more usual in speaking.

example.de: Ich helfe gern, unter der Bedingung, dass wir früh anfangen.
example.en: I am happy to help, on the condition that we start early.

cards.more: Think of a traffic light with a small extra sign under it. Green is yes, red is no, and the extra sign is the condition: yes, but only if. Unter einer Bedingung is that small sign. Das ist übertrieben is a sign that says: too much, please slow down. With such short signs you steer the discussion without shouting. Everybody understands them quickly, so the evening does not take hours.

rows: Ich bin dafür, aber unter einer Bedingung: Wir fragen zuerst die Nachbarn.
Ein ganzes Gründach? Das ist übertrieben!
Das ist unsinnig, weil es niemand braucht.
Ja, aber das Lastenrad ist zu teuer.
Ein Tauschregal ist eine wirksamere Maßnahme als ein Lastenrad.

cards.title: Coming to a result
cards.body: A good discussion ends with a result. The club works in four steps: collect the ideas, talk about advantages and disadvantages, vote, and say what you agreed on. The last step has a fixed chunk: Wir haben uns auf die Aufräumaktion geeinigt. Sich einigen is reflexive.
cards.lead: A discussion without a result is only talk. Frau Weber leads the evening in four steps, and each step has its own phrases. The last step is new today: how to say what the group decided.

examples.de: Zuerst sammeln wir alle Ideen.
examples.en: First we collect all the ideas.

examples.de: Dann sprechen wir über Vorteile und Nachteile.
examples.en: Then we talk about advantages and disadvantages.

examples.de: Wir haben uns auf die Aufräumaktion geeinigt.
examples.en: We have agreed on the clean-up action.

deeper.text: Sich einigen goes with auf and the accusative: Wir haben uns auf einen Termin geeinigt. The little word auf belongs to the verb, so learn the two together. When everybody agrees, you can also say Wir sind uns einig. That sentence describes the situation, and the Perfekt with geeinigt describes the decision that has been made.

example.de: Wir sind uns einig: Die Aufräumaktion kommt zuerst.
example.en: We agree: the clean-up action comes first.

cards.more: Think of choosing a film with friends. First everybody names films, then you talk about which one is too long or too scary, then you vote with a show of hands, and finally someone says: So, we are watching this one. That last sentence is the result. In German it is Wir haben uns auf den Film geeinigt. The club does the same with the four ideas, only the topic is the neighbourhood.
steps: 1. Ideen sammeln: every idea goes on the board.
2. Vorteile und Nachteile besprechen: einerseits … andererseits …
3. Abstimmen: Wer ist dafür? Wer ist dagegen?
4. Das Ergebnis sagen: Wir haben uns auf die Aufräumaktion geeinigt.

cards.title: Polite disagreement in German
cards.body: In German discussions people often say what they think directly. Das sehe ich anders is normal and not rude, because it only names your opinion. If you want to sound softer, first agree a little: Da hast du recht, aber … or Ich verstehe dich, aber … The phrases differ in tone, not in meaning.
cards.lead: Learners worry that a direct no is impolite. The table shows how German speakers disagree in a normal discussion, and how you can soften the tone when you want to.

examples.de: Das sehe ich anders.
examples.en: I see that differently.

examples.de: Da hast du recht, aber das Lastenrad ist zu teuer.
examples.en: You are right there, but the cargo bike is too expensive.

examples.de: Ich verstehe dich, aber ich bin trotzdem dagegen.
examples.en: I understand you, but I am against it all the same.

deeper.text: Das sehe ich anders states your view, and Da hast du recht, aber … first gives the other person a point. The second softens the disagreement. In Austria people often soften even more, for example with the Konjunktiv: Ich würde das vielleicht anders sehen. Mira, who is from Wien, often speaks like this. This is a tendency only. People differ a lot everywhere.

example.de: Ich würde das vielleicht anders sehen.
example.en: I would perhaps see that differently.

cards.more: Imagine two ways of knocking on a door. One person knocks twice, clearly: tock tock. Another knocks softly and says good evening first. Both people want to come in, and both are polite. Das sehe ich anders is the clear knock, and Da hast du recht, aber is the soft knock with the greeting. In a club evening you can use either. Choose the soft one when you do not know the others well.

rows: in any discussion, it is not rude
you want to keep it friendly
better avoid it with people you do not know

lessons.title: Sonne, Wolken, Föhn: weather words and D-A-CH
lessons.goal: Describe weather precisely with es and weather verbs, use new weather adjectives, read a short weather report and compare climates in D-A-CH.

grammar.topic: Weather: es with weather verbs and weather adjectives
grammar.point: No new grammar. Weather verbs always take es: es regnet, es schneit, es hagelt, es blitzt, es donnert, also when another word stands first and in every tense. With adjectives you use sein: Es ist neblig. To compare climates use the comparative before a noun with its ending: Madrid hat heißere Sommer als Berlin. After sein the comparative has no ending.

mistake.why: Weather verbs always need es, also when another word is in position 1.

terms.meaning: a dummy subject: es regnet; it never changes and is never left out
a warm, dry wind from the Alps; also the word for the hair dryer

cards.title: Before we start: from 'Es regnet' to 'Es gibt Schauer und Gewitter'
cards.body: Weather is the most reliable small talk in Germany. You can already say Es regnet or Es ist sonnig. Today you learn to be more exact: shower, hail, lightning, thunder, damp and dry. You also hear what the weather is like in Germany, Austria and Switzerland. This lesson has no new grammar.
steps: You already know: Es regnet. and Es ist sonnig und windig. from earlier chapters.
New today: Es hagelt. and Morgen ist es regnerisch und mild. Exact words for the weather.
By the end you can: describe weather precisely, understand a short weather report and say how climates differ in D-A-CH.

examples.de: Es regnet.
examples.en: It is raining.
examples.why: You know this: es plus a weather verb.

examples.de: Morgen ist es regnerisch und mild.
examples.en: Tomorrow it is rainy and mild.
examples.why: New today: two new weather adjectives.

cards.more: Think of a painter. At the beginning she owns three colours: sun, rain, wind. With three colours she can paint a picture, but not a very exact one. Today she gets a larger box: hail, lightning, fog, damp, mild. With more colours the picture of the weather becomes more precise. You paint the same landscape, only richer. And you learn who in the neighbourhood talks about it most: everybody.

cards.title: Madrid, Wien, München, Berlin
cards.body: Sunday morning in the WG. It rains again, and Leon asks how the weather is where the others come from. Ben talks about Madrid, Mira about Wien, Anna about München. Read the dialogue and notice the comparisons: viel heißer, kälter, feucht and grau.
cards.lead: A rainy morning starts a weather talk. Four cities come up, and each person compares their home with Berlin. Read the eight lines once and underline every weather word that you do not know yet.

examples.de: In Madrid ist der Sommer viel heißer und trockener als in Berlin.
examples.en: In Madrid the summer is much hotter and drier than in Berlin.

examples.de: In Wien sind die Winter kälter als in Madrid.
examples.en: In Wien the winters are colder than in Madrid.

examples.de: In München gibt es manchmal Föhn.
examples.en: In München there is sometimes föhn.

deeper.text: Bei is a small word with a big job: it means at someone's place, or in someone's part of the world. Bei uns in Wien is a very normal way to say in our country or in our city. It lets people compare homes in the same breath: Bei uns ist es anders. You use it with the dative, so bei uns, bei euch, bei Anna.

example.de: Bei uns in Wien ist es im Winter kalt.
example.en: At our place in Wien it is cold in winter.

cards.more: Imagine a world map with four pins: Madrid, Wien, München and Berlin. Each friend puts a small weather card on their pin, and the cards say: hot and dry, cold winter, föhn, damp and grey. That is the scene. When they talk, they walk from pin to pin with the little word als. Look for als in the lines: it is the bridge between two places in each comparison.
steps: Leon: Es regnet schon wieder! Wie ist das Wetter bei euch zu Hause?
Ben: In Madrid ist der Sommer viel heißer und trockener als in Berlin.
Mira: In Wien sind die Winter kälter als in Madrid. Im Winter schneit es dort manchmal.
Anna: In München gibt es manchmal Föhn. Dann bin ich ganz müde.
Leon: Was ist Föhn?
Anna: Ein warmer, trockener Wind aus den Alpen. Viele Menschen sind dann wetterfühlig.
Ben: Und in Berlin? Hier ist es oft feucht und grau.
Mira: Heute ist es besonders nass. Hoffentlich wird es morgen heiter.

cards.title: Weather verbs with es
cards.body: Weather verbs have no real doer. They always take es: es regnet, es schneit, es hagelt, es blitzt, es donnert, es friert. With the adjective version you use sein: es ist neblig. The little word es is never missing, also when another word stands in first position.
cards.lead: The first lines already used es regnet and es schneit. This card gathers the verbs for a storm and for winter. Most of them are short and follow the normal pattern, so learning them takes only a minute.

examples.de: Im Winter schneit es oft.
examples.en: In winter it often snows.

examples.de: Zuerst blitzt es, dann donnert es.
examples.en: First there is lightning, then there is thunder.

examples.de: Heute hagelt es sogar.
examples.en: Today it is even hailing.

deeper.text: This es is a dummy subject: it does not stand for any thing, but the sentence needs a subject. It never changes, in any tense: es regnet, es hat geregnet, es wird regnen. Do not try to drop it or to replace it. The English it works in the same way: it rains, it rained. That makes the rule easy to remember.

example.de: Gestern hat es den ganzen Tag geregnet.
example.en: Yesterday it rained the whole day.

cards.more: Picture a stage play with a very quiet actor. In a story about people, each verb has an actor who does something. But who rains? Nobody. Still the stage manager wants an actor on the stage, so a small figure called es walks on and stands there. He does nothing, he only fills the place. He wears the same costume in all tenses. If you try to play the scene without him, the audience feels something is missing.

cards.title: Weather adjectives in pairs
cards.body: Adjectives describe the air and the sky. Many come in pairs. feucht means damp and its opposite is trocken. mild means not cold, regnerisch means with a lot of rain, and heiter describes a nice sky with only a few clouds. You use all of them with es ist or with the noun.
cards.lead: With the verbs you say what falls from the sky. With adjectives you describe what the day is like. The table gives you four pairs and a typical sentence for each, so that you can place them in a weather report.

examples.de: Im Herbst ist die Luft in Berlin oft feucht.
examples.en: In autumn the air in Berlin is often damp.

examples.de: Morgen ist es regnerisch und mild.
examples.en: Tomorrow it is rainy and mild.

examples.de: Das Wetter bleibt heiter und trocken.
examples.en: The weather stays fair and dry.

deeper.text: The word heiter lives a double life. Das Wetter ist heiter means few clouds and nice, and it is the word in forecasts. But Ben ist heute sehr heiter means that Ben is cheerful. Same word, two uses, and the context shows which one is meant. With a person it describes a mood, with the weather it describes the sky.

example.de: Ben ist heute sehr heiter.
example.en: Ben is very cheerful today.

cards.more: Think of a wardrobe with two sides. On the left side you hang the clothes for dry days, on the right side those for damp days. A pair like feucht and trocken works like these two rails: whenever you pick one word, the other one is next to it. Mild is the jacket for the middle, regnerisch is the umbrella. When you learn weather words in pairs, you always remember two for the price of one.

rows: In Madrid ist der Sommer trocken.
Der Winter ist dieses Jahr mild.

cards.title: The weather report
cards.body: A weather report is short and full of nouns: Temperatur, Schauer, Gewitter, Blitz and Donner. It names the time of day first and then the weather. Die Temperatur is given in Grad. Read the small report on this card and look for the time words: heute, am Nachmittag, morgen, übermorgen.
cards.lead: Now the words work together. Here is a short report, as you might hear it on the radio after the news. Read it line by line and find the time of day, the weather and the temperature in each line.

examples.de: Am Nachmittag gibt es Schauer.
examples.en: In the afternoon there are showers.

examples.de: Am Abend gibt es ein Gewitter mit Blitz und Donner.
examples.en: In the evening there is a thunderstorm with lightning and thunder.

examples.de: Morgen sind es zwölf Grad.
examples.en: Tomorrow it will be twelve degrees.

deeper.text: A forecast often gives an approximate or a limit value. Um neun Grad means around nine degrees. Bis zu vierzehn Grad means not more than fourteen. In writing you see digits and the sign °C, in speaking people say Grad: neun Grad. Below zero, they say minus drei Grad. So the small words um and bis zu carry the exact information.

example.de: Am Tag wird es bis zu vierzehn Grad warm.
example.en: During the day it gets up to fourteen degrees.

cards.more: Think of a train timetable, but for the sky. Every line has a time, a destination and a note. In the weather timetable the time is heute or morgen, the destination is the kind of weather, and the note is the temperature. If you read it like a timetable, from left to right and line by line, you find what you need in seconds. You will get this quickly, even in a quick radio voice.
steps: Wetterbericht für Berlin:
Heute: bewölkt, um neun Grad. Am Nachmittag gibt es Schauer.
Heute Abend: ein Gewitter mit Blitz und Donner. Dazu ist es windig.
Morgen: mild, zwölf Grad, trocken, am Abend neblig.
Übermorgen: heiter und trocken, nachts kalt.

cards.title: Weather in D-A-CH
cards.body: Weather reports in Germany, Austria and Switzerland all use degrees Celsius. Some weather words are regional. Der Föhn is a warm, dry wind from the Alps, and many people say they are wetterfühlig. Aprilwetter means changing weather. Schmuddelwetter is colloquial for grey, wet and cold. In Swiss German es schiffet means it rains.
cards.lead: Weather is also culture. Each region has its own weather words and its own habits of talking about the weather. This card collects five facts that help you understand what people mean when they chat in the lift.

examples.de: Viele Menschen sind bei Föhn wetterfühlig.
examples.en: Many people are sensitive to the weather when there is föhn.

examples.de: Im April ist oft Aprilwetter: Sonne, Regen und Wind.
examples.en: In April it is often changeable weather: sun, rain and wind.

examples.de: Bei Schmuddelwetter bleiben viele lieber zu Hause.
examples.en: In grey, wet weather many people prefer to stay at home.

deeper.text: Der Föhn is also the word for the hair dryer. The wind came first, and the device took its name, because it also blows warm, dry air. The device is written Föhn or Fön, both are said the same way. Germans know which one is meant from the situation, so a hair dryer in the bathroom is never confused with the Alps.

example.de: Mira trocknet die Haare mit dem Föhn.
example.en: Mira dries her hair with the hair dryer.

cards.more: Imagine you fly over Europe with a weather map. In the north you see grey clouds and drizzle, in the south the mountains with a warm wind rolling down. Each place has a word for what you see. Föhn belongs to the mountains, Schmuddelwetter to the grey cities, Aprilwetter to spring and es schiffet to Switzerland. When you hear one of these words, you also hear where the speaker comes from.

cards.title: Comparing climates
cards.body: Climate describes the usual weather over many years. To compare it you use the comparative before a noun, with the ending you know: heißere Sommer, kältere Winter. After the comparative you put als and the other place. In the Alps you also find a special wind: In den Alpen gibt es manchmal Föhn.
cards.lead: The last card puts weather and comparison together. You describe how places differ, and you use the comparative before a noun, which you learned in lesson 1, now with plural nouns and weather words.

examples.de: In den Alpen gibt es manchmal Föhn.
examples.en: In the Alps there is sometimes föhn.

examples.de: Madrid hat heißere Sommer als Berlin.
examples.en: Madrid has hotter summers than Berlin.

examples.de: Wien hat kältere Winter als Madrid.
examples.en: Wien has colder winters than Madrid.

deeper.text: Compare two patterns. After sein the comparative has no ending: Im Sommer ist es in Madrid heißer als in Berlin. After haben, before a noun, it gets the ending: Madrid hat heißere Sommer als Berlin. The meaning is the same, but the shape of the word changes. Ask yourself: is there a noun right behind the adjective? If yes, add the ending.

example.de: Im Sommer ist es in Madrid heißer als in Berlin.
example.en: In summer it is hotter in Madrid than in Berlin.

cards.more: Imagine two suitcases standing side by side: one packed for Madrid, one for Wien. In the Madrid case lie light clothes for hot summers, in the Wien case warm jackets for cold winters. The sentence pattern is the label on the handle: Madrid hat heißere Sommer, Wien hat kältere Winter. The little word als is the arrow between the two cases. Pack the sentence the same way each time and you will never forget it.
steps: Place A + hat + comparative + plural noun + als + place B.
Madrid hat heißere Sommer als Berlin.
Wien hat kältere Winter als Madrid.
After sein: no ending. Im Sommer ist es in Madrid heißer als in Berlin.

grammar.point: No new grammar. A forecast uses es wird …, es soll … (they say) and laut Wetterbericht …. For your own feeling use mir ist kalt, not es ist mir kalt. Compare days with the comparative or superlative before a noun and the normal ending: ein wärmerer Tag, der heißeste Tag des Jahres.

cards.title: Before we start: from 'Es ist kalt' to 'Morgen soll es kälter werden'
cards.body: On Saturday the whole street wants to clean the river bank, so everybody asks one question: how is the weather? You already say Es wird kalt and Es ist wärmer als gestern. Today you learn to read and give a forecast, to talk about extreme weather and to make small talk. There is no new grammar, only use.
steps: You already know: Es wird kalt. and Es ist wärmer als gestern.
New today: Laut Wetterbericht soll es ab 15 Uhr Schauer geben. A forecast with its typical phrases.
By the end you can: understand a forecast, compare days, say you are cold and give a weather tip with damit or um … zu.

examples.de: Es wird kalt.
examples.en: It is getting cold.
examples.why: You know this: es wird plus an adjective.

examples.de: Laut Wetterbericht soll es ab 15 Uhr Schauer geben.
examples.en: According to the weather report there should be showers from 3 pm.
examples.why: New today: a forecast sentence with soll.

cards.more: Think of the weather report as a short news story about tomorrow. A news story has a source and a promise: according to someone, something will happen. You already tell stories with es wird. Today you add the source: laut Wetterbericht, and the careful verb soll, which means it is said so. Then you can talk about Saturday without sounding sure, exactly as a real forecaster does. Nobody can promise sunshine, but everybody can report what the experts say.

cards.title: Planning the action day
cards.body: Frau Weber and Mira plan the clean-up on Saturday and check the forecast. Read the dialogue and look for the times of day: morgens, mittags and ab 15 Uhr. Each time has its own weather, so a forecast always has three parts.
cards.lead: The weather decides whether the action works. In this short dialogue Mira reads the forecast to Frau Weber. Listen for the order: first the morning, then noon, then the afternoon, each with its own weather.

examples.de: Morgens sind es acht Grad, und es ist bewölkt.
examples.en: In the morning it is eight degrees, and it is cloudy.

examples.de: Mittags wird es sonnig, bei vierzehn Grad.
examples.en: At noon it is getting sunny, at fourteen degrees.

examples.de: Ab 15 Uhr soll es Schauer geben.
examples.en: From 3 pm there should be showers.

deeper.text: In forecasts the time word often stands in first position: Morgens …, Mittags …, Ab 15 Uhr … . Then the verb comes second and es follows it. The ending -s on a time of day (morgens, mittags, abends) means regularly or at that time of day. This order is why forecasts sound so short and clear: time, verb, es, weather.

example.de: Abends wird es kühler.
example.en: In the evening it is getting cooler.

cards.more: Imagine a weather map on the television: the day is cut into three slices, a bit like a cake. The first slice is morning, the second noon, the third afternoon. The speaker points at one slice after the other and puts the weather on it: grey, sunny, wet. Your dialogue does the same with words. When you plan something outside, always ask yourself what the weather does in each slice, because one slice can ruin everything.
steps: Frau Weber: Mira, wie wird das Wetter am Samstag? Wir machen doch die Aufräumaktion am Spreeufer.
Mira: Ich habe gerade die Vorhersage gelesen. Morgens sind es acht Grad, und es ist bewölkt.
Frau Weber: Und mittags?
Mira: Mittags wird es sonnig, bei vierzehn Grad. Aber ab 15 Uhr soll es Schauer geben.
Frau Weber: Dann sind wir um 13 Uhr fertig. Hoffentlich bleibt es trocken!
Mira: Laut Wetterbericht ja. Ich nehme lieber eine Regenjacke mit.

cards.title: Forecast language
cards.body: A forecast uses a few fixed phrases. Es wird … tells what the weather becomes. Es soll … reports what others say. Laut Wetterbericht … names the source. The temperature can steigen or fallen: Die Temperaturen steigen. Degrees below zero are minus fünf Grad.
cards.lead: The dialogue used soll and wird in the same lines. This card puts the typical forecast phrases side by side, so you can recognise each one on the radio and use it yourself when you plan something.

examples.de: Morgen wird es kälter.
examples.en: Tomorrow it will get colder.

examples.de: Es soll morgen regnen.
examples.en: It is supposed to rain tomorrow.

examples.de: Nachts sind es minus fünf Grad.
examples.en: At night it is minus five degrees.

deeper.text: Soll here is not a duty. In a forecast, sollen reports what other people say: the weather service, the radio, a neighbour. Es soll regnen means They say it will rain, and the speaker does not promise it. You only need this use inside weather chunks. For orders you meet sollen later in other meanings, but the forecast one is the most common.

example.de: Es soll morgen schneien.
example.en: They say it will snow tomorrow.

cards.more: Compare it with a friend who tells you gossip. Es wird kälter is what you say when you look out of the window yourself: you see it. Es soll kälter werden is what you say when you only heard it from someone: you do not see it. Laut Wetterbericht gives the name of that someone, like a note under a news story. So the three phrases tell the listener how sure you are, which is useful in every plan.

rows: Nachts sind es minus fünf Grad.
Es sind um die zehn Grad.

cards.title: Extreme weather
cards.body: Some weather is not only pleasant or unpleasant, it is dangerous or unusual. The Hitzewelle is a long hot time, the Dürre a long dry time. Glatteis is a thin, invisible layer of ice on the street. Frost is a temperature below zero. Hochwasser means that a river is too high.
cards.lead: Forecasts and news often use stronger words than sonnig or regnerisch. This card gives you five of them, with the typical situation for each one, so that you understand a warning when you hear it.

examples.de: Im Sommer gibt es manchmal eine Hitzewelle.
examples.en: In summer there is sometimes a heatwave.

examples.de: Bei Glatteis fahre ich nicht mit dem Fahrrad.
examples.en: When there is black ice I do not ride my bike.

examples.de: Nach viel Regen gibt es oft Hochwasser.
examples.en: After a lot of rain there is often high water.

deeper.text: Hochwasser and Überschwemmung are not the same. Hochwasser describes the river: its water is very high. Die Überschwemmung is what happens to the land: the water has left the river bed and covers streets and fields. In the news you hear both together. For you, Hochwasser is enough, and you only need to recognise Überschwemmung.

example.de: Das Hochwasser ist gestern gekommen.
example.en: The high water came yesterday.

cards.more: Look at the words as pictures. A Hitzewelle is a wave of heat that rolls over the country, like a wave in the sea. Die Dürre has the same root as dry and thirsty: the land has too little water. Das Glatteis is smooth (glatt) ice. Hochwasser is simply high water, so the river is too high. If you can see the picture, you do not need to translate the word, and you remember it for a long time.

cards.title: Comparing days
cards.body: You can compare days with the comparative before a noun: ein wärmerer Tag. Add the normal ending after the comparative. For the top of the list use the superlative: der heißeste Tag. With of the year you add the genitive: der heißeste Tag des Jahres.
cards.lead: You compared climates in the last lesson. Now you compare single days, one against another, which is exactly what you do when you plan an action. Watch the ending after the comparative and after the superlative.

examples.de: Samstag wird ein wärmer er Tag als Freitag.
examples.en: Saturday will be a warmer day than Friday.

examples.de: Das war der heißeste Tag des Jahres.
examples.en: That was the hottest day of the year.

examples.de: Mittags ist es wärmer als morgens.
examples.en: At noon it is warmer than in the morning.

deeper.text: After the superlative you say of what with the genitive: der heißeste Tag des Jahres, der kälteste Monat des Jahres, der sonnigste Tag der Woche. Das Jahr is neuter and takes des … Jahres, die Woche is feminine and takes der Woche. In the news this pattern is very common, because journalists love records.

example.de: Der Januar war der kälteste Monat des Jahres.
example.en: January was the coldest month of the year.

cards.more: Imagine a ranking list on a wall with seven days of the week, ordered by temperature. At the bottom stands the coldest day, at the top the hottest. If you only compare two days, you say ein wärmerer Tag als Freitag. If you speak about the whole list, you say der wärmste Tag der Woche. The pattern is the same as for people: older than, the oldest of the group. Weather simply makes a long list of days.
steps: 1 Choose the adjective: warm, heiß, kalt.
2 Comparing two days: comparative + ending: ein wärmerer Tag als Freitag.
3 Top of the list: superlative + ending: der heißeste Tag.
4 Say of what with the genitive: des Jahres, der Woche.

cards.title: Weather small talk
cards.body: Weather is easy small talk with neighbours. You make a remark and add oder to ask for agreement: Schönes Wetter heute, oder? You can also complain together: Ganz schön schwül heute! And you can express hope: Hoffentlich bleibt es trocken. Bei dem Wetter … starts a reason.
cards.lead: In the courtyard, in the lift, at the bus stop: people start a conversation with the weather. This card gives you four short openers and one polite way to answer, so a short talk is easy.

examples.de: Schönes Wetter heute, oder?
examples.en: Nice weather today, isn't it?

examples.de: Ganz schön schwül heute!
examples.en: Quite humid today!

examples.de: Bei dem Wetter bleibe ich lieber zu Hause.
examples.en: With this weather I prefer to stay at home.

deeper.text: Small talk about the weather is normal in Germany, Austria and Switzerland, but people often do it less with strangers than in Britain. It is common with neighbours, colleagues and in the lift. Ganz schön plus an adjective means quite a lot: ganz schön kalt. It is a friendly way to complain without a real problem.

example.de: Heute ist es aber eisig, oder?
example.en: It is icy today, isn't it?

cards.more: Think about a very short game of tennis. Somebody hits the ball with a weather remark: Schönes Wetter heute, oder? The other person has to hit it back, with ja, stimmt or a small complaint. The game lasts only three or four hits, and then both go on with their day. Nobody wants a long talk about clouds. The point is only to say hello in a friendly way, and the weather is the safest ball.

cards.title: Mir ist kalt: feeling or weather?
cards.body: There are two ways to be cold. Es ist kalt describes the weather. Mir ist kalt describes how you feel. The little word mir is the feeling person. For heat it is the same: Es ist heiß is the weather, Mir ist heiß is you. Never say Es ist mir kalt.
cards.lead: After the forecast comes the question of how you feel. German makes a clear difference between weather and body. This card shows the two sentence types next to each other, so you do not mix them up.

examples.de: Es ist kalt heute.
examples.en: It is cold today (the weather).

examples.de: Mir ist heute kalt.
examples.en: I feel cold today.

examples.de: Mir ist im Sommer oft zu heiß.
examples.en: In summer I often feel too hot.

deeper.text: The verb frieren says the same as Mir ist kalt, but with a doer: Ich friere. It is used for a longer or stronger feeling of cold: Ich friere seit einer Stunde. Mir ist kalt is very common for a short feeling. In both versions you can ask the other person: Frierst du? or Ist dir kalt? Both questions are friendly.

example.de: Ben friert schnell, denn er kommt aus Madrid.
example.en: Ben gets cold quickly, because he comes from Madrid.

cards.more: Think of two switches. The first switch is outside: it shows what the weather does. With this switch you use es. The second switch is on your body: it shows what you feel. With this one you use mir, as in a medical report: To me, it is cold. The two switches can show different things at the same time. Outside it can be warm, but you can still feel cold if you have a fever.

cards.title: Dressing for the weather
cards.body: Weather talk often ends in a tip: what to take or wear. You know the goal forms. Same person doing both: um … zu. Different persons: damit. Nimm eine Regenjacke mit, damit du nicht nass wirst. Ich ziehe eine Mütze an, um nicht zu frieren.
cards.lead: A forecast is useful only if it changes what you do. This last card uses your two goal patterns from the chapter in short tips about clothes, so the new weather words and the old grammar work together.

examples.de: Nimm eine Regenjacke mit, damit du nicht nass wirst.
examples.en: Take a rain jacket so that you do not get wet.

examples.de: Ich ziehe eine Mütze an, um nicht zu frieren.
examples.en: I put on a hat in order not to freeze.

examples.de: Mira nimmt Handschuhe mit, damit es allen warm ist.
examples.en: Mira takes gloves so that everybody is warm.

deeper.text: Note the difference in the sentences: um … zu names a goal of the same person (ich ziehe an, um nicht zu frieren), damit needs a new subject or a new focus (damit du nicht nass wirst). With a weather verb the damit-clause often gets es as its subject: damit es warm ist. In the damit-clause the conjugated verb stands at the end.

example.de: Wir bringen Tee mit, damit es allen warm bleibt.
example.en: We bring tea so that everybody stays warm.

cards.more: Imagine a packing list for Saturday. Next to every item you write the reason in a few words: Regenjacke, damit du nicht nass wirst. Mütze, um nicht zu frieren. Wasser, damit alle genug trinken. A tip with a reason is easier to accept than a simple order, because people can see why. And a reason in German always has its verb in a clear place: at the end of damit-sentences, or as zu plus a verb after um.
steps: 1 Check the forecast for the three times of day.
2 Decide what you need: Regenjacke, Mütze, Handschuhe.
3 Same person: ... , um nicht zu frieren.
4 Other person: ... , damit du nicht nass wirst.

lessons.title: Lebensmittel retten: Foodsharing
lessons.goal: Understand and talk about commitment for people and nature using Foodsharing as an example: commitment verbs, reasons with um … zu and damit, and invitations to join.

grammar.topic: Commitment: sich engagieren für, reasons with um … zu and damit
grammar.point: No new grammar. Sich engagieren and sich einsetzen take für + accusative. Helfen takes the dative. Give a reason with um … zu (the same person) or damit (a new subject, verb at the end). To invite use Hast du Lust mitzumachen?

terms.meaning: a movement since 2012 in Germany where volunteers save food and share it for free
a public shelf or fridge where free food is shared
unpaid, as a volunteer

cards.title: Before we start: from 'Ich helfe im Verein' to 'Ich engagiere mich für …'
cards.body: Every Tuesday morning, Leon saves bread that a bakery cannot sell. Nobody pays him. It is a good example of Engagement, a word you will hear often in Germany. You already know ehrenamtlich and der Verein. Today you learn the verbs for commitment and the reasons people give. There is no new grammar, only use.
steps: You already know: ehrenamtlich, der Verein, sich interessieren für.
New today: Leon engagiert sich für Foodsharing. Er rettet Brot, damit es nicht im Müll landet.
By the end you can: say what you commit to, give a reason with um … zu or damit and invite someone to join in.

examples.de: Ich interessiere mich für Musik.
examples.en: I am interested in music.
examples.why: You know this: a reflexive verb with für.

examples.de: Leon engagiert sich für Foodsharing.
examples.en: Leon is committed to Foodsharing.
examples.why: New today: the same pattern with a new verb.

cards.more: In many countries people say I volunteer at a charity. German has a richer word, Engagement, for any unpaid effort for others or for nature. Someone who engagiert sich does more than a hobby: they give their time, because they think something is important. You can say it about a neighbour who helps the old lady next door, or a student who cleans a river bank. The nice thing is that the sentence pattern is the same as for sich interessieren für.

cards.title: Leon's Tuesday
cards.body: Read the short text about Leon's Tuesday. It shows the whole story in simple sentences: early start, bakery, bicycle, shelf. Look for the goal of his work and for the word for the shelf, the Fairteiler.
cards.lead: This chapter now moves from weather to people. The text is short and uses only the present tense and words you know, plus one new word, Fairteiler. Read it once for the story and once for the reasons.

examples.de: Jeden Dienstag holt Leon Brot in einer Bäckerei ab.
examples.en: Every Tuesday Leon picks up bread in a bakery.

examples.de: Er bringt das Brot zum Nachbarschaftshaus.
examples.en: He brings the bread to the neighbourhood house.

examples.de: Leon legt das Brot ins Regal, damit jeder etwas findet.
examples.en: Leon puts the bread on the shelf so that everybody finds something.

deeper.text: For repeated times, German uses the accusative without a preposition: jeden Dienstag, jeden Tag, jede Woche. The ending shows the accusative: jeden for masculine, jede for feminine. In English you say every Tuesday and never need a word like on. With a fixed day of the week you can also say dienstags, which means every Tuesday and sounds a little more formal.

example.de: Mira fährt jede Woche zweimal zur Arbeit.
example.en: Mira goes to work twice every week.

cards.more: Imagine the text as a little film with six scenes. In scene one Leon gets up early. In scene two he stands in the bakery, in scene three he carries two bags. Scene four shows the bicycle ride, scene five the shelf with the bread, scene six a smile. Each scene has one sentence, and the reasons are the music in the background. If you watch the film in your head, the sentences stay in your memory.
steps: Jeden Dienstag steht Leon früh auf.
Um sieben Uhr holt er in einer Bäckerei Brot ab, das übrig ist.
Die Bäckerin gibt ihm zwei große Tüten.
Dann fährt er mit dem Fahrrad zum Nachbarschaftshaus.
Dort steht der Fairteiler, ein Regal für Lebensmittel.
Leon legt das Brot ins Regal, damit jeder etwas findet.
Alles ist kostenlos. Leon macht das ehrenamtlich, er bekommt kein Geld.

cards.title: What is Foodsharing?
cards.body: Foodsharing is a movement that began in Germany in 2012. Volunteers, called Foodsaver or Lebensmittelretter, collect food that shops would throw away. They share it for free, for example in a Fairteiler, a public shelf or fridge. Nobody earns money, it is ehrenamtlich.
cards.lead: Leon's text mentioned the Fairteiler and doing everything for free. This card explains the idea behind it: where Foodsharing comes from, who does it and where the food goes. All facts are short and clear.

examples.de: Foodsharing gibt es in Deutschland seit 2012.
examples.en: There has been Foodsharing in Germany since 2012.

examples.de: Freiwillige holen Lebensmittel ab, die sonst im Müll landen.
examples.en: Volunteers collect food that would otherwise end up in the bin.

examples.de: Das Essen im Fairteiler ist kostenlos.
examples.en: The food in the Fairteiler is free.

deeper.text: Foodsharing is not the same as die Tafel. The Tafel helps people with little money: they get food at special points. Foodsharing saves food for everyone, whoever you are and however much money you have. Both are ehrenamtlich and both fight waste, but the people they help are different. In many towns they even work together.

example.de: Die Tafel hilft Menschen mit wenig Geld.
example.en: The Tafel helps people with little money.

cards.more: Think of a public bookshelf in the street. Anyone can take a book and anyone can leave one. The Fairteiler works the same way, only with food: bread, fruit, vegetables. A volunteer fills it, a neighbour takes what they need and nobody asks questions. The name itself is a play on words: teilen means to share, and fair means just. So the shelf shares food in a fair way, and nothing goes into the bin.

rows: a food-saving movement, since 2012 in Germany
a public shelf or fridge for free food

cards.title: Verbs of commitment
cards.body: To say what you commit to, use sich engagieren für or sich einsetzen für, both with the accusative. For people in need you can also use helfen with the dative: Ich helfe der Nachbarin. Retten means to save. The question is Wofür engagierst du dich?
cards.lead: The text and the facts showed a commitment. Now you get the verbs to talk about it. Two of them are reflexive and take für, like sich interessieren für. The others are simple and you can use them at once.

examples.de: Leon engagiert sich für Foodsharing.
examples.en: Leon is committed to Foodsharing.

examples.de: Frau Weber setzt sich für den Kiez ein.
examples.en: Frau Weber stands up for the neighbourhood.

examples.de: Wofür engagierst du dich?
examples.en: What do you commit yourself to?

deeper.text: Sich engagieren is used for commitment without pay, like a volunteer job or a good cause. For a paid job you say arbeiten für: Mira arbeitet für eine kleine Softwarefirma. If you try hard to reach something, the verb is sich bemühen um, which you only need to recognise. To answer Wofür? you can say Dafür, dass …: Ich engagiere mich dafür, dass der Kiez sauber bleibt.

example.de: Ich engagiere mich dafür, dass der Kiez sauber bleibt.
example.en: I am committed to keeping the neighbourhood clean.

cards.more: Picture a person holding a banner. They stand for something: für Foodsharing, für den Kiez. In German the little word für is on the banner, always followed by the accusative. Sich einsetzen is the same picture with a push: you put your whole body into the cause. Retten is the strongest verb, like a lifeguard: you save something from falling into the bin. And helfen only needs a person in the dative: Ich helfe dir.

rows: Er setzt sich für den Kiez ein.

cards.title: Why people do it
cards.body: People who engage give reasons. For their own goal they use um … zu: Ich mache mit, um etwas gegen Verschwendung zu tun. For a result for other people they use damit: Ich hole Brot ab, damit andere es essen. Both patterns are old friends from this chapter.
cards.lead: A commitment always has a reason: why does someone get up early to carry bread? This card gives two typical reasons, one with each of your purpose patterns, and shows when to choose which.

examples.de: Ich mache mit, um etwas gegen Verschwendung zu tun.
examples.en: I join in to do something against waste.

examples.de: Ich hole Brot ab, damit andere es essen.
examples.en: I pick up bread so that others eat it.

examples.de: Wir helfen mit, um die Natur zu schützen.
examples.en: We help in order to protect nature.

deeper.text: Many names in German movements are English: Foodsaver, Start-up, Carsharing. They often sound modern, are short and travel across countries, so a group can use the same name everywhere. German speakers use them like normal nouns with an article: das Start-up, das Carsharing, der Foodsaver. Inside the sentence they behave like German words, and the plural often takes -s or stays the same.

example.de: Zwei Studentinnen gründen ein Start-up.
example.en: Two students found a start-up.

cards.more: Think of two lines on a sign. The first line says what I want: I join in, to do something against waste. The second line says what you get: I pick up bread, so that you can eat it. If I am the only person in the sentence, I use um and zu. If somebody else enters the sentence, I use damit and put the verb at the end. A quick check: can I replace the goal with I want to? Then um … zu works.
steps: 1 Who wants to reach the goal? Only me: um … zu.
2 Somebody else appears in the goal: damit.
3 Um: zu plus the infinitive at the end (um … zu tun).
4 Damit: a new subject, the verb at the end.

cards.title: People and nature
cards.body: Engagement helps people or nature, and often both. For people there is Nachbarschaftshilfe and the Tafel. For nature there is Naturschutz and the Aufräumaktion. Foodsharing does both: it gives people food and avoids waste. The table puts the two sides next to each other.
cards.lead: Until now we looked at Leon. Many other people in the Kiez engage for other things. This card sorts typical activities into two groups so you can answer when somebody asks what a project is for.

examples.de: Die Nachbarschaftshilfe hilft Menschen im Viertel.
examples.en: The neighbourhood help helps people in the district.

examples.de: Die Aufräumaktion schützt die Natur.
examples.en: The clean-up protects nature.

examples.de: Foodsharing hilft Menschen und der Natur.
examples.en: Foodsharing helps people and nature.

deeper.text: An association can be gemeinnützig. That means non-profit: it works for the common good and does not want to earn money. Because of this, the state often gives it a tax advantage. Many Vereine in Germany are gemeinnützig, for example sports clubs, the Tafel and local groups. When you see this word on a poster, you know that the money goes into the cause.

example.de: Der Verein ist gemeinnützig.
example.en: The association is non-profit.

cards.more: Draw two columns on a sheet of paper. On the left write people, on the right write nature. Now put each project you know in the column where it helps most: Nachbarschaftshilfe left, Naturschutz right. Then notice that some projects stand in the middle, like Foodsharing, because they help both. This sorting game is a good way to talk about any group: ask yourself who or what benefits, and the sentence writes itself.

cards.title: Asking someone to join
cards.body: To invite someone, you ask: Hast du Lust mitzumachen? For an easy start you say: Jeder kann mitmachen. Man braucht nur Zeit und Lust. The verb mitmachen is separable, so zu stands inside: mitzumachen. With Frau Weber or Herr Ali you say Haben Sie Lust mitzumachen?
cards.lead: A commitment grows when people join. This last card gives three short sentences to invite someone, to say that everybody is welcome and to explain what is needed, all in a friendly tone.

examples.de: Hast du Lust mitzumachen?
examples.en: Do you feel like joining in?

examples.de: Jeder kann mitmachen.
examples.en: Everybody can join in.

examples.de: Man braucht nur Zeit und Lust.
examples.en: You only need time and desire.

deeper.text: Lust haben works in two ways. With zu plus infinitive you name an activity: Hast du Lust mitzumachen? With auf you name a thing: Hast du Lust auf Suppe? Notice the polite form: with people you say Sie to, use Haben Sie Lust …? and keep the rest the same. Lust is a friendly word, not a rude one, and in this phrase it only means desire.

example.de: Haben Sie Lust auf eine Suppe?
example.en: Would you like some soup?

cards.more: Imagine standing next to a table where people sort bread. Somebody walks past and looks interested. You do not want to push, so you ask in a light way: Hast du Lust mitzumachen? If the person says no thanks, nothing is lost. If they say yes, you hand over a pair of gloves. Short, friendly and without pressure: this is how many neighbourhood groups find new helpers, and the three chunks are all you need.
